                                                    Question 248

                                                    Convert the infix expression A + B * C - D / E to postfix.

                                                      Source

                                                      • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 31

                                                      Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                      Use the cited definitions and invariants to distinguish the requested concept from related operations.

                                                      Study-guide sections

                                                      DSA13 · Infix, postfix and prefix expressions

                                                      Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                      Study-guide references

                                                      DSA13 · Infix, postfix and prefix expressions

                                                      Answer: ABC*+DE/-

                                                      DSA13 works the exact expression. Multiplication groups B*C and division groups D/E before addition and subtraction. Emit A, then B C *, then +, then D E /, then −, producing ABC*+DE/-.

                                                      Evidence in the complete study note

                                                      Infix places an operator between operands and uses precedence and parentheses. Prefix places it first; postfix places it last. Their fixed operator arity determines grouping. To convert infix to postfix, output operands immediately and hold operators on a stack. Pop higher-precedence operators before pushing a new operator; also pop equal precedence for left-associative operators. Parentheses temporarily override this order.DSA13
                                                      A+B*C-D/E becomes ABC*+DE/-.DSA13

                                                      Question 249

                                                      What condition causes stack overflow in an array-implemented stack?

                                                        Source

                                                        • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 32

                                                        Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                        Use the cited definitions and invariants to distinguish the requested concept from related operations.

                                                        Study-guide sections

                                                        DSA11 · Implement a stack with one consistent top convention

                                                        Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                        Study-guide references

                                                        DSA11 · Implement a stack with one consistent top convention

                                                        Answer: Attempting push when the fixed array is full.

                                                        DSA11 distinguishes full storage from the overflow attempt. Under zero-based top-as-last-occupied convention, full means top=C−1; a count convention uses size=C. A push must check this before writing beyond capacity.

                                                        Evidence in the complete study note

                                                        Stack policy is LIFO, equivalently FILO. Push inserts, pop removes/returns top, and peek only observes. With zero-based occupied slots, top=-1 is empty and top=C-1 is full. Check before A[++top]=x or returning A[top--].DSA11
                                                        Overflow is an attempted insertion into full storage; underflow is an attempted removal from empty storage.DSA11

                                                        Question 250

                                                        What are the three main operations of a Stack and their time complexities?

                                                          Source

                                                          • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 33

                                                          Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                          State the representation and cost model, then count the operations or storage demanded by the question.

                                                          Study-guide sections

                                                          DSA11 · Implement a stack with one consistent top convention

                                                          Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                          Study-guide references

                                                          DSA11 · Implement a stack with one consistent top convention

                                                          Answer: Push, pop, and peek are O(1) for fixed-array or head-linked stacks.

                                                          DSA11 defines push insertion, pop removal/return, and peek observation at top. Fixed-array indexing and linked-head updates take constant work. A resizing append or singly linked tail-pop implementation can change the cost, so the guarantee needs the stated representations.

                                                          Evidence in the complete study note

                                                          Stack policy is LIFO, equivalently FILO. Push inserts, pop removes/returns top, and peek only observes. With zero-based occupied slots, top=-1 is empty and top=C-1 is full. Check before A[++top]=x or returning A[top--].DSA11
                                                          A count-based alternative uses size=0 and A[size++]=x. Do not combine its empty/full tests with the top-index convention. Fixed-array push/pop are constant time. Linked stacks achieve constant time by inserting and deleting at the head; using a singly linked tail for pop would require a predecessor traversal.DSA11

                                                          Question 251

                                                          In postfix notation, why are parentheses unnecessary?

                                                            Source

                                                            • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 34

                                                            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                            Use the cited invariant or operation rule, state its assumptions, and trace a small case to justify the result.

                                                            Study-guide sections

                                                            DSA13 · Infix, postfix and prefix expressions

                                                            Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                            Study-guide references

                                                            DSA13 · Infix, postfix and prefix expressions

                                                            Answer: Operator position and known arity determine grouping.

                                                            DSA13 places postfix operators after their operands. During stack evaluation, each binary operator consumes the two latest operand values in right-then-left order and pushes their result. The sequence therefore encodes grouping without precedence parentheses.

                                                            Evidence in the complete study note

                                                            Infix places an operator between operands and uses precedence and parentheses. Prefix places it first; postfix places it last. Their fixed operator arity determines grouping. To convert infix to postfix, output operands immediately and hold operators on a stack. Pop higher-precedence operators before pushing a new operator; also pop equal precedence for left-associative operators. Parentheses temporarily override this order.DSA13
                                                            To evaluate postfix, push operands. At a binary operator, pop right operand first, then left, and push left op right. Build an expression tree for either prefix (preorder) or postfix (postorder); a stack is useful but is not the only possible conversion representation.DSA13

                                                            Question 252

                                                            What is the difference between a simple array queue and a circular queue?

                                                              Source

                                                              • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 35

                                                              Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                              Use the cited invariant or operation rule, state its assumptions, and trace a small case to justify the result.

                                                              DSA15 · Circular buffers: logical order differs from physical slots

                                                              Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                              Study-guide references

                                                              DSA15 · Circular buffers: logical order differs from physical slots

                                                              Answer: Circular wraparound reuses freed front slots; a simple noncircular queue may not.

                                                              DSA15 distinguishes a rear index reaching the array end from circular modulo arithmetic. A circular queue can insert into positions freed at the front, while a simple noncircular version may report overflow despite those gaps. Capacity and empty/full conventions still must be consistent.

                                                              Evidence in the complete study note

                                                              A simple noncircular array queue may report overflow when rear reaches the final index despite released slots at the front. A circular queue reuses slots with modulo arithmetic. Use a count convention: front points to the next removal, size counts items, and insertion slot is (front+size)%C. Empty means size==0; full means size==C.DSA15

                                                              Question 253

                                                              A stable priority queue serves smaller numeric priority keys first and compares equal priorities by an increasing arrival counter, also smallest first. If two tasks have equal priority, in what order are they served?

                                                                Adapted from

                                                                • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 36

                                                                Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                Use the cited invariant or operation rule, state its assumptions, and trace a small case to justify the result.

                                                                Study-guide sections

                                                                DSA17 · Priority queues serve by priority, with an explicit tie rule

                                                                Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                Study-guide references

                                                                DSA17 · Priority queues serve by priority, with an explicit tie rule

                                                                Answer: FIFO among equal priorities: the task that arrived earlier is served first.

                                                                The priority comparison ties, so the specified comparator proceeds to the arrival counter. An increasing counter gives the earlier arrival the smaller secondary key, causing it to be removed first. Equal-priority tasks are therefore served FIFO under this stable policy. That result follows from the explicitly chosen tie rule; an ordinary priority queue without a stability or comparator rule would not inherently guarantee arrival-order service.

                                                                Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                Arrays and lists can also implement priority queues: an unordered sequence gives cheap insertion but linear extremum removal; an ordered sequence reverses that tradeoff. Equal priorities have no inherent FIFO guarantee. If stable service is required, compare (priority, arrival_counter). Choose the priority direction and tie rule before tracing.DSA17

                                                                    Question 256

                                                                      DSA19 · BST search follows a global ordering invariant

                                                                      Answer: Every left-subtree key is smaller and every right-subtree key larger, for distinct keys.

                                                                      DSA19 imposes this invariant over entire subtrees at every node, not only immediate children.                                                                         Question 258

                                                                        When deleting a BST node with two children, what are the two valid replacement choices?

                                                                          Source

                                                                          • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 41

                                                                          Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                          DSA21 · BST deletion preserves every subtree restriction

                                                                          Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                          Study-guide references

                                                                          DSA21 · BST deletion preserves every subtree restriction

                                                                          Answer: Inorder predecessor or inorder successor.

                                                                          DSA21 identifies the maximum key in the left subtree and minimum key in the right subtree as valid replacement values. Copy one into the deleted node, then remove that value’s original node, which has at most one child. These preserve the subtree order invariant.

That second deletion has at most one child.DSA21

                                                                          Question 259

                                                                          What is the time complexity of BST search in the best case vs worst case?

                                                                            Source

                                                                            • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 42

                                                                            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                            Use the cited invariant or operation rule, state its assumptions, and trace a small case to justify the result.

                                                                            Study-guide sections

                                                                            DSA19 · BST search follows a global ordering invariant

                                                                            DSA22 · Balanced trees prevent the sorted-input chain

                                                                            Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                            Study-guide references

                                                                            DSA19 · BST search follows a global ordering invariant

                                                                            DSA22 · Balanced trees prevent the sorted-input chain

                                                                            Answer: Best successful search Θ(1); arbitrary BST worst Θ(n), balanced worst Θ(log n).

                                                                            DSA19 gives a constant root hit and O(height) search. A chain has linear height, producing linear worst work; logarithmic height disciplines in DSA22 improve that worst bound. Calling every BST logarithmic would incorrectly assume balance.

                                                                            Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                            Search compares at each node and follows one child until equality or null. Insertion uses that same path to attach a new leaf. Operations cost O(height): logarithmic for balanced trees, linear for a chain. Best-case successful search is Theta(1), a root hit. An optimal BST minimizes expected search cost using access probabilities; constructing it is a different problem from searching it.DSA19
                                                                            AVL balance factor is height(left)-height(right); every node must have factor -1,0 or 1. After insertion or deletion, update heights upward and rotate where necessary. LL imbalance needs a right rotation; RR needs left; LR rotates the left child left then the node right; RL is symmetric. Rotations preserve inorder key order.DSA22

                                                                              DSA42 · DFS: finish a branch before returning

                                                                              Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                              Study-guide references

                                                                              DSA41 · BFS: discover one distance layer at a time

                                                                              DSA42 · DFS: finish a branch before returning

                                                                              Answer: BFS explores distance layers with FIFO; DFS finishes branches with a stack or recursion.

                                                                              DSA41 enqueues discoveries in layer order, while DSA42 resumes the latest unfinished branch before later neighbors. Both can traverse all reachable vertices, but their pending-work discipline and visitation order differ. BFS also has the unweighted minimum-edge guarantee.

                                                                              Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                              Mark the source when enqueuing it. Repeatedly dequeue a vertex, examine its neighbours, and enqueue each unvisited neighbour while marking it. Store predecessor[v] when discovering v if a path must be reconstructed. FIFO ensures vertices at distance d are explored before later distance layers.DSA41
                                                                              Mark a vertex, then recursively visit each unmarked neighbour before continuing with later neighbours. An explicit stack can store pending work instead. Both implement latest-pending-work first; a queue would change that discipline. Marking prevents infinite repetition around graph cycles.DSA42

                                                                              Question 261

                                                                              A directed graph has edges with direction; an undirected graph does not. Give one real-world example of each.

                                                                                Source

                                                                                • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 44

                                                                                Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                Use the cited invariant or operation rule, state its assumptions, and trace a small case to justify the result.

                                                                                Study-guide sections

                                                                                DSA40 · Graphs: represent the relationships you actually need

                                                                                Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                Study-guide references

                                                                                DSA40 · Graphs: represent the relationships you actually need

                                                                                Answer: Directed: following accounts; undirected: a mutual friendship relationship.

                                                                                DSA40 gives following as directed because u following v need not imply v following u. It gives mutual friendship as undirected, representing a symmetric connection. The examples concern relation semantics rather than whether lines happen to be drawn with arrows.

                                                                                Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                A graph has vertices V and edges E. Directed edges distinguish u→v from v→u; undirected edges represent two-way relationships. Following accounts is directed; a mutual friendship relation is undirected. Weighted edges carry costs; unweighted shortest-path questions count edges. DAG expands to directed acyclic graph. Trees are connected acyclic graphs, although graph data structures may also contain cycles.DSA40

                                                                                Question 262

                                                                                Why is a dense graph more computationally expensive to process than a sparse graph?

                                                                                  Source

                                                                                  • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 45

                                                                                  Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                  Use the cited invariant or operation rule, state its assumptions, and trace a small case to justify the result.

                                                                                  Study-guide sections

                                                                                  DSA40 · Graphs: represent the relationships you actually need

                                                                                  DSA41 · BFS: discover one distance layer at a time

                                                                                  Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                  Study-guide references

                                                                                  DSA40 · Graphs: represent the relationships you actually need

                                                                                  DSA41 · BFS: discover one distance layer at a time

                                                                                  Answer: Edge-processing algorithms do more work when E is larger.

                                                                                  DSA40 says dense simple graphs approach quadratic edge counts and adjacency lists use Θ(V+E) space. Traversals or algorithms inspecting every edge therefore require more work as density increases. This is not universal: a vertex-only operation need not inspect edges.

                                                                                  Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                  A matrix uses Theta(V²) space and constant edge lookup. Adjacency lists use Theta(V+E) space and enumerate neighbours. Dense simple graphs approach quadratic edge counts. Examining every edge costs more on denser graphs; vertex-only operations need not inspect every edge.DSA40
                                                                                  BFS finds minimum-edge paths in unweighted graphs, not arbitrary minimum-weight paths. With adjacency lists it costs O(V+E); scanning a matrix costs O(V²). To traverse a disconnected graph, restart from each unvisited vertex. Neighbour order affects tied traversal order but not minimum distances.DSA41

                                                                                  Question 263

                                                                                  In a full binary tree, every node has either 0 or 2 children. How does this differ from a complete binary tree?

                                                                                    Source

                                                                                    • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 46

                                                                                    Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                    Use the cited invariant or operation rule, state its assumptions, and trace a small case to justify the result.

                                                                                    Study-guide sections

                                                                                    DSA18 · Tree vocabulary and the different binary shapes

                                                                                    Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                    Study-guide references

                                                                                    DSA18 · Tree vocabulary and the different binary shapes

                                                                                    Answer: Full restricts each node to zero or two children; complete restricts level filling.

                                                                                    DSA18 defines full by each node’s child count and complete by filled earlier levels plus left-filled final level. Those are distinct conditions: completeness can allow one child at the boundary, while fullness alone need not keep every level filled.

                                                                                    Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                    Binary means at most two children. Full means each node has zero or two children. Complete means all earlier levels are filled and the last fills from left. Perfect means all leaves share a level and every internal node has two children. Balanced means height stays logarithmic under a stated rule; it does not require a perfect shape.DSA18

                                                                                    Question 264

                                                                                    What distinguishes a weighted graph from an unweighted graph, and when would you prefer weighted?

                                                                                      Source

                                                                                      • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 47

                                                                                      Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                      Use the cited invariant or operation rule, state its assumptions, and trace a small case to justify the result.

                                                                                      Study-guide sections

                                                                                      DSA40 · Graphs: represent the relationships you actually need

                                                                                      DSA43 · Shortest paths and spanning trees solve different objectives

                                                                                      Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                      Study-guide references

                                                                                      DSA40 · Graphs: represent the relationships you actually need

                                                                                      DSA43 · Shortest paths and spanning trees solve different objectives

                                                                                      Answer: Weighted edges carry differing costs; use them when edge costs matter.

                                                                                      DSA40 assigns costs to weighted edges and says unweighted shortest-path questions count edges. Distances or travel costs can therefore justify weights when fewer edges is not the true objective. DSA43 then distinguishes weighted shortest paths from unweighted BFS.

                                                                                      Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                      A graph has vertices V and edges E. Directed edges distinguish u→v from v→u; undirected edges represent two-way relationships. Following accounts is directed; a mutual friendship relation is undirected. Weighted edges carry costs; unweighted shortest-path questions count edges. DAG expands to directed acyclic graph. Trees are connected acyclic graphs, although graph data structures may also contain cycles.DSA40
                                                                                      For nonnegative weights, standard Dijkstra initializes source distance zero and others infinity, repeatedly finalizes the unsettled vertex with smallest distance, and relaxes each outgoing edge: dist[v]=min(dist[v],dist[u]+w(u,v)). A min-priority queue supports the next choice. BFS is enough when every edge has equal cost; negative edges require another justified method, such as Bellman–Ford.DSA43

                                                                                      Question 265

                                                                                      If a BST receives keys in sorted order (1,2,3,4,5), what shape does the tree take and what is the search complexity?

                                                                                        Source

                                                                                        • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 48

                                                                                        Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                        Use the cited invariant or operation rule, state its assumptions, and trace a small case to justify the result.

                                                                                        Study-guide sections

                                                                                        DSA19 · BST search follows a global ordering invariant

                                                                                        Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                        Study-guide references

                                                                                        DSA19 · BST search follows a global ordering invariant

                                                                                        Answer: An ordinary unbalanced insertion forms a right chain; worst search is Θ(n).

                                                                                        DSA19 explicitly traces sorted insertion 1,2,3,4,5 into a right chain. Each new larger key follows right links to the tail, making the height linear. Worst search follows that chain, while a root hit remains constant. Balanced insertion would rotate and is a different assumption.

                                                                                        Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                        Search compares at each node and follows one child until equality or null. Insertion uses that same path to attach a new leaf. Operations cost O(height): logarithmic for balanced trees, linear for a chain. Best-case successful search is Theta(1), a root hit. An optimal BST minimizes expected search cost using access probabilities; constructing it is a different problem from searching it.DSA19
                                                                                        Sorted insertions 1,2,3,4,5 instead form a right chain.DSA19

                                                                                        Question 266

                                                                                        When would you choose a linked list over an array? Give a specific scenario.

                                                                                          Source

                                                                                          • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 1

                                                                                          Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                          Use the cited invariant or operation rule, state its assumptions, and trace a small case to justify the result.

                                                                                          Study-guide sections

                                                                                          DSA10 · Doubly linked, circular and practical list choices

                                                                                          DSA02 · Arrays: indexed access, capacity and shifting

                                                                                          Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                          Study-guide references

                                                                                          DSA10 · Doubly linked, circular and practical list choices

                                                                                          DSA02 · Arrays: indexed access, capacity and shifting

                                                                                          Answer: Choose links for frequent known-location updates, such as a doubly linked history cursor.

                                                                                          DSA10 gives browser history with a doubly linked cursor as an application. With references to current insertion or removal positions, link changes avoid shifting an array’s later elements; arbitrary positional lookup can still be linear. This concrete scenario supports the choice without claiming universal superiority.

                                                                                          Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                          Lists suit changing sequences when references to insertion positions are already available. Finding a position is still linear. Lists can hold polynomial terms (coefficient, exponent), directory or block links, child lists in nonbinary trees, and hash chains. Browser history can use a doubly linked cursor. A playlist may be circular; airline seat lookup requires a specified seat-record model, not an automatic linked-list answer.DSA10
                                                                                          A fixed array has a chosen capacity; the choice need not occur at compile time. A resizable array allocates a larger block and copies when needed. Inserting in the middle shifts later elements, so it costs linear time. Appending into spare capacity is constant; a resizing append can be linear, though repeated geometric growth gives amortized constant append cost.DSA02

                                                                                          Question 267

                                                                                          How does a stack differ from a queue? Give an application for each.

                                                                                            Source

                                                                                            • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 2

                                                                                            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                            Use the cited invariant or operation rule, state its assumptions, and trace a small case to justify the result.

                                                                                            Study-guide sections

                                                                                            DSA11 · Implement a stack with one consistent top convention

                                                                                            DSA14 · Queues preserve arrival order

                                                                                            DSA12 · Trace stack operations and reversible actions

                                                                                            Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                            Study-guide references

                                                                                            DSA11 · Implement a stack with one consistent top convention

                                                                                            DSA14 · Queues preserve arrival order

                                                                                            DSA12 · Trace stack operations and reversible actions

                                                                                            Answer: Stack: LIFO for undo; queue: FIFO for equal-priority printer jobs.

                                                                                            DSA11 gives latest-first stack service and DSA12 applies it to undoing the latest edit. DSA14 gives arrival-order queues for equal-priority printing. Both ADTs may use arrays or nodes; their service order, not that representation, is the distinction.

                                                                                            Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                            Stack policy is LIFO, equivalently FILO. Push inserts, pop removes/returns top, and peek only observes. With zero-based occupied slots, top=-1 is empty and top=C-1 is full. Check before A[++top]=x or returning A[top--].DSA11
                                                                                            FIFO suits equal-priority printer jobs, shared-resource waiting, asynchronous buffers and level-order exploration. A play sequence can also use a queue. Distinguish airline seat records from waiting requests; an application name alone does not force one representation.DSA14
                                                                                            Undo moves the latest action from undo to redo; redo moves it back.DSA12

                                                                                            Question 268

                                                                                            Why is a balanced BST (like AVL) preferred over a regular BST? Explain the worst-case scenario.

                                                                                              Source

                                                                                              • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 3

                                                                                              Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                              Use the cited invariant or operation rule, state its assumptions, and trace a small case to justify the result.

                                                                                              Study-guide sections

                                                                                              DSA22 · Balanced trees prevent the sorted-input chain

                                                                                              DSA19 · BST search follows a global ordering invariant

                                                                                              Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                              Study-guide references

                                                                                              DSA22 · Balanced trees prevent the sorted-input chain

                                                                                              DSA19 · BST search follows a global ordering invariant

                                                                                              Answer: Balance prevents linear-height chains and guarantees logarithmic worst search.

                                                                                              DSA22 maintains AVL balance factors through rotations that preserve inorder. DSA19 shows ordinary sorted insertion producing a chain, where a search can traverse all nodes. Maintaining logarithmic height prevents that worst degradation, though root-hit best time remains constant.

                                                                                              Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                              AVL balance factor is height(left)-height(right); every node must have factor -1,0 or 1. After insertion or deletion, update heights upward and rotate where necessary. LL imbalance needs a right rotation; RR needs left; LR rotates the left child left then the node right; RL is symmetric. Rotations preserve inorder key order.DSA22
                                                                                              Search compares at each node and follows one child until equality or null. Insertion uses that same path to attach a new leaf. Operations cost O(height): logarithmic for balanced trees, linear for a chain. Best-case successful search is Theta(1), a root hit. An optimal BST minimizes expected search cost using access probabilities; constructing it is a different problem from searching it.DSA19

                                                                                              Question 269

                                                                                              What is a hash collision? Name two methods to resolve collisions and compare them.

                                                                                                Source

                                                                                                • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 4

                                                                                                Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                                Use the cited invariant or operation rule, state its assumptions, and trace a small case to justify the result.

                                                                                                Study-guide sections

                                                                                                DSA26 · Resolve collisions and watch the load factor

                                                                                                Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                                Study-guide references

                                                                                                DSA26 · Resolve collisions and watch the load factor

                                                                                                Answer: A collision maps different keys to one home address; compare chaining and open addressing.

                                                                                                DSA26 stores colliding entries in bucket lists for chaining, whereas open addressing probes other array slots. Chaining uses link or bucket overhead and expected O(1+α) work; probing keeps entries inside the table and requires careful load and deletion policies. Neither prevents all collisions.

                                                                                                Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                                Separate chaining stores colliding entries in a bucket list. Load alpha=n/m is average chain length; expected operations are O(1+alpha) under suitable distribution assumptions, with O(n) worst cases. Open addressing keeps entries inside the array and probes until a key or an available slot is found.DSA26
                                                                                                Linear probing tries (h(k)+j)%m. For size 7 and keys 10,17,24, all home addresses are 3 and occupied positions become 3,4,5. Quadratic probing changes the step; double hashing uses h1(k)+j h2(k), modulo m, with a step relatively prime to m to cover all slots. Neither method guarantees no collisions. Deletion needs tombstones or reinsertion so searches do not stop prematurely.DSA26

                                                                                                Question 270

                                                                                                What is the difference between BFS and DFS? Which finds the shortest path?

                                                                                                  Sources

                                                                                                  • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 5

                                                                                                  • Algorithm Design & Analysis review questions · Question 4

                                                                                                  Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                                  Use the cited invariant or operation rule, state its assumptions, and trace a small case to justify the result.

                                                                                                  Study-guide sections

                                                                                                  DSA41 · BFS: discover one distance layer at a time

                                                                                                  DSA42 · DFS: finish a branch before returning

                                                                                                  DSA43 · Shortest paths and spanning trees solve different objectives

                                                                                                  Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                                  Study-guide references

                                                                                                  DSA41 · BFS: discover one distance layer at a time

                                                                                                  DSA42 · DFS: finish a branch before returning

                                                                                                  DSA43 · Shortest paths and spanning trees solve different objectives

                                                                                                  Answer: BFS uses FIFO layers and finds shortest unweighted paths; DFS uses branch-first stack order.

                                                                                                  DSA41 guarantees minimum-edge paths for BFS on unweighted graphs. DSA42 says DFS paths are reachability witnesses but need not be shortest. Differing edge weights require an appropriate weighted-path algorithm, such as Dijkstra under nonnegative weights.

                                                                                                  Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                                  BFS finds minimum-edge paths in unweighted graphs, not arbitrary minimum-weight paths. With adjacency lists it costs O(V+E); scanning a matrix costs O(V²). To traverse a disconnected graph, restart from each unvisited vertex. Neighbour order affects tied traversal order but not minimum distances.DSA41
                                                                                                  Using the same graph and alphabetical neighbours, recursive DFS can discover A,B,D,C. Its path is a valid reachability witness but not necessarily shortest. Adjacency-list cost is O(V+E), with O(V) visited state and possible stack depth. DFS supports cycle and connectivity analysis; a directed cycle test distinguishes active recursion vertices from already completed ones.DSA42
                                                                                                  BFS is enough when every edge has equal cost; negative edges require another justified method, such as Bellman–Ford.DSA43

                                                                                                  Question 271

                                                                                                  A text editor needs to implement multi-level undo. Which data structure is most appropriate and why?

                                                                                                    Source

                                                                                                    • Data Structures & Algorithms review questions · Question 6

                                                                                                    Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                                    Use the cited invariant or operation rule, state its assumptions, and trace a small case to justify the result.

                                                                                                    Study-guide sections

                                                                                                    DSA12 · Trace stack operations and reversible actions

                                                                                                    Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                                    Study-guide references

                                                                                                    DSA12 · Trace stack operations and reversible actions

                                                                                                    Answer: Use an undo stack, with a second redo stack if needed.

                                                                                                    DSA12 moves the latest action from undo to redo and reverses that movement for redo. Pushing each new edit and popping for undo naturally matches the most-recent-edit-first requirement. A new edit after undo normally clears redo history.

                                                                                                    Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                                    Calls nest on a runtime stack; the latest call returns first. Bracket matching pushes opening brackets and matches each closing bracket against top. Reversal pushes input then pops it. Undo moves the latest action from undo to redo; redo moves it back. A new edit after undo normally clears redo. DFS and backtracking use the same latest-pending-choice discipline.DSA12
